contentBboxMm.note: Customer uploaded an A4 (210x297mm) source to the 1000x550mm DTF Large template, then scaled the canvas element up to 778.8x548mm. The PRIMARY regression guard is page1WidthPt/HeightPt above (page must be 1000x550mm ≈ 2834x1559pt, NOT A4 595x842pt). Secondary content guards (minWidthMm=200, minHeightMm=400): rendered artwork must occupy at least 200x400mm — proves the canvas scale-up was honored, not partially regressed. If DTF passthrough regresses and ships the source as-is, content would be capped near source A4 (~210x297mm) and fail minHeightMm. If the generator partially scales, the wider minWidthMm/minHeightMm pair catches it.

Placed on the wide 1000x550mm DTF Large template so the landscape A3 source fits without capping/overflow (on a narrow portrait template the multi-up sheet overflows and clips). The source is a multi-up sheet (two columns of Flahavan's logos) whose true inked region is ~160x290mm — the rest of the page is whitespace. Output must not be blank or clipped: feImage-heavy artwork (40 feImage regions) must rasterise the full-height (~290mm) two-column content. Mins kept conservative (120x200) because detected upload bounds vary 395-420mm wide depending on whether the gs-fallback or inkscape path wins under load.

assertions.note: DUAL LOCK for two real flahavans-cap regressions. (1) gs-fallback-crop: this file forces a canvas fallback PNG; checkFallbackAspect requires that PNG's aspect ≈ the detected bounds aspect (1.361). If the gs bbox fallback regresses to a cropped/full-page strip the fallback PNG aspect drifts and this goes red. (2) pdf2svg feImage 1.2x page inflation: the file's MediaBox is landscape A3 (420x297mm) and true content is 395x290mm; uploadBoundsMm maxWidthMm=425/maxHeightMm=305 keep detected bounds inside the MediaBox+tolerance, so if the feImage filter-region inflation (~1.2x → ~474x348mm) returns, the MediaBox clamp regression is caught here.

contentBboxMm.note: Full crest including the white bottom text must render — proves no bottom-band clip from gs under-reporting white ink or from the svg zero-origin normalisation translate.

assertions.note: WHITE-ON-DARK lock (Kilkenny County Council crest, white text along the bottom, on a dark garment). gs -sDEVICE=bbox under-reports white/light ink and historically returned a cropped landscape strip → wrong crop + portrait↔landscape flip. The fix trusts inkscape --query-all unless ONE element dominates the page (>85%). Detected bounds must come back ≈100x94mm (near-square, aspect ~1.066), NOT a wide strip. Compare against fixture 18 (identical artwork, black text) — both MUST report the same bounds; if white drifts away from black, gs under-reporting has regressed.

COUNTER-TEST to fixture 17. Identical crest with BLACK text (gs reads black ink fine, so bounds were always correct here). Detected bounds must equal the white-text twin (≈100x94mm). This guards against an OVER-correction of the white-on-dark fix: if a future change to the gs-vs-inkscape reconciliation distorts normal (black, gs-correct) artwork, this fixture catches it.

SYNTHETIC alpha-trim-floor lock. Near-full-page green panel (GS coverage ~94% ≥0.92 so the white-content rescue gate is skipped) with a WHITE bar at the extreme BOTTOM edge that gs -sDEVICE=bbox cannot see (white ink on gs's white render page). True visible content is 838x1182pt (~295.6x417mm); gs-only stops at 838x1120pt (~395mm tall) and clips the white bar. minHeightMm=410 fails on the gs-only clip and passes once the unconditional alpha-trim floor expands the committed bounds to cover ALL visible content. Counter-balanced by fixtures 17/18 (must not over-grow correct artwork).

WHITE-ON-WHITE no-clip lock (Schembri Batteries, pure-white art on a landscape A4 page, 841.89x595.276pt). gs -sDEVICE=bbox returns 0 0 0 0 (white ink is invisible on gs's white render page) and the old fallback read `inkscape --query-all | head -1` (the root <svg>), but pdf2svg feImage/clip filter regions inflate AND mis-place that root box so the content claimed it touched the page top/right; the zero-origin normalisation then shifted the artwork out of the viewBox and clipped ~35pt off the bottom-right both on the canvas and in the output. The fix renders the ORIGINAL pdf to a transparent raster and alpha-trims it for the TRUE artwork extent. Detected upload bounds must be ~278.4x182.1mm (aspect ~1.53), NOT a page-sized/origin-hugged box. skipPlace=true models the real "upload → generate" flow (single auto-created centered element) so the saved output is clean; outputContentAspect then locks the OUTPUT artwork aspect (measured white-aware via pngalpha+trim) to ~1.53 — a clip/squish/overflow regression drifts this number and goes red. Must route through the standard (non-large-format) bounds path — keep templateId a normal template, not dtf-large.
